title: Twitch Streamer
service: Identity, merch, 3D stream scenes, emotes, subscriber badges
intro: A complete identity for a Twitch channel on its way to becoming a full-time job, from the logo to the emotes to fully 3D stream scenes. Retro-futurist nostalgia, built to feel sleek rather than dated.
brief: Tristan wanted to level up his streaming as a step towards making it his career. He needed a unique, memorable style that reflected his love of retro-futurism and classic vintage games, while still feeling sleek and modern. It also had to be flexible enough to stretch across every kind of media, from streaming assets to merch.
did: The logo started from his initials, TYA, which he wanted present but not too obvious. After working through several variations, we landed on a single continuous stroke that runs through all three letters. Turned vertical, it reads almost like a hieroglyph, which gave the channel a second, more compact mark. A tight palette of near-black, white, a soft purple and a honey yellow, plus a stepped line motif taken from the logo's curve, tie everything else together.

Because the channel lives on its community, a lot of the work went into the things viewers carry around in chat. The subscriber badges tell a small story: a single honeycomb cell at one month grows into a full comb, a jar, a pot, a hive and finally bees, so loyalty is something you can watch evolve. The emotes give regulars a shared language of inside jokes, and a reason to subscribe that directly supports the streamer.

For the stream itself, I designed starting, intermission and ending scenes using 3D modelling alongside graphic design, so that switching between games and activities feels smooth instead of abrupt. A vintage CRT computer, glitching pop-up windows and synthwave wireframe landscapes carry the retro-futurist mood all the way through to the final drive into the sunset.
